events.title: Magellan Enters the Pacific
events.description: After navigating the treacherous strait at South America's southern tip, Ferdinand Magellan's fleet sailed out into the open ocean beyond. The crossing had taken weeks of storms, mutiny and hardship.
events.significance: The passage opened a sea route between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. It became a key step in the first circumnavigation of the globe.

events.title: The Royal Society Is Conceived
events.description: After a lecture at Gresham College in London, twelve men decided to form a society for promoting physical and mathematical learning. They included Christopher Wren and Robert Boyle.
events.significance: This group grew into the Royal Society, one of the world's oldest and most influential scientific academies.

events.title: Panama Declares Independence from Spain
events.description: Panama broke from Spanish rule and joined Gran Colombia, the federation led by Simón Bolívar's allies. The date is still celebrated as a national holiday.
events.significance: The declaration was a turning point in Panama's history and part of the wave of independence movements across Latin America.

events.title: The Tehran Conference Begins
events.description: US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Tehran for the first time as the 'Big Three'. They discussed how to coordinate the war against Nazi Germany.
events.significance: The talks shaped Allied military strategy, including the planned invasion of France, and the postwar world that followed.

events.title: NASA Launches Mariner 4 to Mars
events.description: Mariner 4 lifted off on a mission to fly past the Red Planet. It became the first spacecraft to take close-up photographs of another planet.
events.significance: Its images of a cratered Martian surface changed scientific ideas about Mars and proved that interplanetary probes could work.
